 Order
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner with a prayer to direct the opposite parties,
specifically opposite party no.2, the Collector, Jajapur and opposite party no.3, the Land Acquisition Officer (NH-20 Cell), Collector, Jajpiur to take appropriate decision on the application of the petitioner under Annexures-3 and 4 and disburse the compensation/solatium in favour of the petitioner in respect of the construction made over the land in question within a stipulated period.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has submitted an application before the Collector, Jajpur, opposite party no.2 which is purported to one under section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (hereafter '2013 Act') and therefore, the Collector, Jajpur should have referred the matter to the authority.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
However,
on going through the application filed by the petitioner, this Court finds that there is no such prayer in that application.

It is open to the petitioner to file appropriate application under section 64 of 2013 Act before the opposite party no.2, the Collector, Jajpur with the certified copy of this order and in that event, the Mursid Ali Khan vs State Of Odisha And on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178243594/
1 opposite party no.2 shall do the needful in accordance with law.

entities.text: Mursid Ali Khan vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the application submitted by the petitioner.
Accordingly, the writ petition stands disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy as per Rules.
